content_html:
Every year, Cusco becomes the scene of one of the most impressive religious celebrations in Peru: the Corpus Christi. This festival, which combines Catholic spirituality and Andean tradition, attracts thousands of local and foreign visitors who seek to experience the authenticity of Cusco culture.

When is Corpus Christi celebrated in Cusco?

The Cusco Corpus Christi is celebrated 60 days after Easter Sunday. In 2025, the central date will be Thursday June 19, although the activities begin several days before.

The route of the saints: procession, music and devotion

During the celebration, 15 religious images —among saints and virgins— are carried in procession from the churches of the traditional neighborhoods to the Cusco Cathedral, in the Plaza de Armas. The litters are huge and beautifully decorated with flowers, embroidery, gold and silver leaf.

The streets are filled with music, dance and popular devotion. It is a moment where The Catholic faith and Andean rituals coexist, creating a unique experience in the world.

Gastronomic tradition: chiriuchu, the emblematic dish

The chiriuchu, a typical dish of this festival, is another protagonist. This cold food brings together ingredients from the three regions of Peru (guinea pig, chicken, chorizo, seaweed, corn, cheese, among others) and is traditionally consumed around the plaza during Corpus Christi.

A unique experience in the Peruvian Andes

live the Corpus Christi in Cusco It is more than attending a procession: it is immersing yourself in centuries of history, a mix of cultures and a living expression of religious syncretism in the Andes. If you plan to travel to Peru in June, don't miss this unforgettable festivity.

Travel tip: Book accommodation in advance, as the city receives thousands of tourists during these dates. If you require more information, you can count on GT Peru Travel We plan and develop a unique adventure for your trip.
